page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.e-c1m4.2xlarge is an entry-level shared-tier virtual instance from the ecs.e server family. Built on an x86_64 Intel Xeon processor running at 2.5 GHz, it supplies 8 shared vCPUs distributed across 4 physical cores with multithreading support. The configuration includes 32.0 GB of memory, establishing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. It comes with no bundled local storage disks and zero GPU hardware accelerators, relying on network-attached storage and operating over a 1 Gbps baseline network interface managed via a KVM hypervisor.

Performance benchmarks indicate a separation between single-threaded and multi-threaded capabilities. Single-core benchmarks demonstrate lower-tier output, marked by weak scores in single-core stress-ng (1103.48) and Geekbench single-core (927.0), alongside low throughput in single-threaded gzip and bzip3 decompression. Conversely, multi-threaded workloads utilize the 8 shared vCPUs effectively, achieving middle-tier results with a multi-core stress-ng metric of 8359.56, a Geekbench multi-core score of 4623.0, and 8008.0 in Clang compilation. Large block uncached memory bandwidth sustains 59.29 GB/sec read and 48.19 GB/sec write speeds.

With its shared CPU architecture and lack of dedicated cores, the instance trades deterministic per-core compute isolation for high resource density. It delivers moderate throughput on standard server metrics, reaching 7.54 GB/sec in static web serving and 11.04 million operations per second in Redis SET tests, while PassMark database operations remain in the lower quartile. This hardware profile is appropriate for general-purpose workloads, distributed web application tiers, staging environments, microservices, and asynchronous task runners that do not require high single-thread clock execution or integrated local NVMe storage.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.e-c1m4.2xlarge is a shared general-purpose virtual instance in the ecs.e family. Powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon processor operating at 2.5 GHz, the server delivers 8 shared vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores with multithreading, paired with 32.0 GB of memory. It does not include local disk storage or GPU accelerators, and it features a 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmark data reflects subdued single-core execution, with Geekbench single-core and single-threaded compression tests rating in the lower percentiles. In contrast, multi-threaded tasks demonstrate middle-tier efficiency, yielding an average Geekbench multi-core score of 4623.0 and stress-ng multi-core rating of 8359.56. Static web serving reaches 7.54 GB/sec, while Redis SET operations sustain 11.04 million operations per second. The server offers a cost-effective allocation of memory and vCPUs appropriate for general-purpose workloads, microservices, staging setups, and distributed web serving where dedicated core performance is unnecessary.
